doc: This reads a bit like a press release, but yeah, the number is grim. Whatever side people are on, kids being killed at that rate should make everyone stop hand-waving it away. It’s worse than looking away, a lot of governments are basically giving stern little speeches then carrying on as normal. You can argue about Hamas all day, but dead children on this scale shouldn’t be waved off as some unavoidable bit of war. Agreed on the urgency, though I wish people would say it plainer. Whatever the military argument is, if the answer leaves thousands of children dead in a few weeks then the answer is broken. You can't dress that up as just unfortunate maths. It's wild how we outsourced all our manufacturing capacity and now we're realizing we can't just print physical goods when we actually need them.

It's absolutely devastating. The fact that the international community can just stand by and watch this happen is infuriating. Exactly. The gap between political promises and actual industrial capacity is embarrassing. It takes years to scale up production lines, and they should have started this back in 2022.

These numbers are absolutely devastating. It's insane how the international community can just look the other way while this happens. Yeah. At some point the number is the whole argument. You can’t just keep calling dead kids collateral and act like that explains it away.

Yeah, if numbers like this don’t force a ceasefire push, what exactly would? Kids are not military targets. This is just unbearable. It's absolutely devastating. The sheer scale of the loss is hard to wrap your head around, and there's no end in sight.

It really is sickening. The double standards and lack of action from world leaders is just infuriating to watch. The kids part is what makes it impossible to scroll past. Whatever people think the military goal is, this many children dead in three weeks is just obscene. It's wild how we forgot that physical stuff actually has to be built. You can't just print money and expect shells to magically appear on the front lines. That is absolutely heartbreaking. It's wild how some people still try to downplay the scale of what's actually happening over there.

We spent decades offshoring all our actual tool-and-die shops, and now we're realizing you can't just train a whole generation of specialized machinists overnight. That child displacement number is the part that sticks with me. People talk about territory maps, but for families this means school years blown apart, parents trying to work from temporary housing, kids bouncing between countries and relatives. Even if the shooting stopped tomorrow, that damage does not just tidy itself up. “Less urgent” feels like a pretty dangerous way to phrase it. Russia doesn’t stop launching missiles just because the inventory spreadsheet is awkward. Air defence is one of those things where you find out you needed it yesterday.

Yeah, the timing is the bit people keep smoothing over. New shifts and contracts help, but they don't magically create propellant, machines, trained workers and QA capacity by spring. 2022 was when the boring factory decisions mattered. Which UN report says that? Ukraine is horrific, but casualty comparisons across Gaza, Sudan, Ethiopia spillover etc get messy fast depending on whether you mean civilians, soldiers, or total deaths. Air defence is the boring bit that decides a lot of the war now. Patriots/SAMP-T for ballistic missiles, NASAMS/IRIS-T for cruise missiles and drones, plus enough interceptors to keep them firing. The hardware matters, but the missile stockpile is the real choke point.

Altering direct quotes from elected officials is a new low, even for Fox. That's just straight up lying and spreading misinformation. Exactly. You can't shoot a treasury bond out of a howitzer. We spent decades dismantling heavy industry and now we can't even scale up basic artillery shell production. It's crazy how quickly things can escalate like this.
